properties.areaDesc: Telfair, GA
properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued May 24 at 6:07PM EDT until May 24 at 6:30PM EDT by NWS Peachtree City GA
properties.description:
SVRFFC

The National Weather Service in Peachtree City has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Southeastern Telfair County in central Georgia...

* Until 630 PM EDT.

* At 607 PM EDT, a severe thunderstorm was located over Horse
Creek Wma, or 11 miles north of Broxton, moving north at 30 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and quarter size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Hail damage to vehicles is expected. Expect wind damage
to roofs, siding, and trees.

* Locations impacted include...
Jacksonville, Towns, Horse Creek Wma, and Workmore.
properties.instruction:
For your protection move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a
building.

If you see wind damage...hail or flooding...wait until the storm has
passed...and then call the National Weather Service toll free
at 1 8 6 6 7 6 3 4 4 6 6 or tweet us your report at NWSATLANTA.

properties.areaDesc: Johnson and Bartlett Mesas Including Raton Pass; Far Northeast Highlands; Union County; Harding County
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued May 24 at 4:06PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
At 406 PM MDT, Doppler radar was tracking a line of showers and
thunderstorms extending from 13 miles southeast of Sugarite to near
Abbott, moving east at 25 mph.

HAZARD...These showers and thunderstorms are producing abrupt wind
gusts of 50 to 55 mph and pea size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor damage to outdoor objects is
possible.

Locations impacted include...
Des Moines, Folsom, Farley, Capulin, Gladstone and Abbott.

This includes Highway 64 between Mile Markers 358 and 395.
properties.instruction:
Monitor the weather situation closely and be alert for threatening
weather conditions.

portion of central Kentucky, including the following areas, Harrison
and Scott.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued May 24 at 6:06PM EDT by NWS Morristown TN
properties.description:

thunderstorms near Dayton, moving northeast at 30 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 40 mph.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects.

Locations impacted include...
Dayton, Decatur, Soddy-Daisy, Spring City, Graysville, Flat Top
Mountain, Peakland, Stinging Fork Falls State Park, Big Spring, and

properties.instruction:

localized flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded
roadways.

Dade City, Ridge Manor, St. Leo, San Antonio, Saint Leo, Lacoochee,

properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued May 24 at 5:05PM CDT until May 24 at 6:00PM CDT by NWS Fort Worth TX
properties.description:
SVRFWD

The National Weather Service in Fort Worth has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Southeastern Montague County in north central Texas...
Northern Wise County in north central Texas...

* Until 600 PM CDT.

* At 505 PM CDT, a severe thunderstorm was located over Alvord, or 10
miles northwest of Decatur, moving northwest at 10 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and quarter size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Hail damage to vehicles is expected. Expect wind damage
to roofs, siding, and trees.

* This severe thunderstorm will be near...
Alvord around 510 PM CDT.
Sunset around 520 PM CDT.

Other locations impacted by this severe thunderstorm include
Fruitland, Park Springs, and Forestburg.
properties.instruction:
For your protection get inside a sturdy structure and stay away from
windows.

Continuous cloud to ground lightning is occurring with this storm.
Move indoors immediately. Lightning can kill.

Heavy rainfall is occurring with this storm, and may lead to flash
flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded roadways.

properties.areaDesc: Dooly; Crisp; Wilcox; Dodge; Telfair
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued May 24 at 6:04PM EDT by NWS Peachtree City GA
properties.description:
At 604 PM EDT, a line of strong thunderstorms was along a line
extending from near Arabi to near China Hill, and moving north at
25 mph.

HAZARD...40 to 50 mph wind, frequent cloud to ground lightning and
heavy rain.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect minor damage to tree limbs and blowing around of
light, unsecured objects. Heavy rain may cause temporary
street flooding especially in poor drainage areas.

Locations impacted include...
Cordele, Vienna, Abbeville, Rochelle, Milan, Arabi, Pineview, Rhine,
Pitts, Jacksonville, Union, Richwood, Seville, China Hill, Pleasant
View, Tippettville, Double Run, Wenona, East Crisp, and Cedar Creek.
properties.instruction:
People outdoors should seek shelter immediately. If you can hear
thunder, you are close enough to be struck by lightning. Motorists
should slow down and be prepared for possible loss of control due to
hydroplaning.

NWSheadline: Strong thunderstorms will impact portions of southern Dodge, western Telfair, Wilcox, southeastern Dooly and Crisp Counties through 630 PM EDT

properties.areaDesc: Dallas, TX; Tarrant, TX
properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued May 24 at 5:03PM CDT until May 24 at 8:15PM CDT by NWS Fort Worth TX
properties.description:
FFWFWD

The National Weather Service in Fort Worth has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Western Dallas County in north central Texas...
Southeastern Tarrant County in north central Texas...

* Until 815 PM CDT.

* At 503 PM CDT, Doppler radar indicated slow moving thunderstorms
producing heavy rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 2
inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 2
inches are forecast. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to
begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets, and underpasses as well as other
poor drainage and low lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Dallas, Fort Worth, Arlington, Irving, Grand Prairie, Mansfield,
Euless, Desoto, Grapevine, Cedar Hill, Duncanville, Burleson,
Lancaster, University Park, Benbrook, Crowley, Forest Hill, Glenn
Heights, Highland Park and River Oaks.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Gale Warning, northeast winds 30 to 40 kt with

vessel for hazardous conditions.

* WHERE...A portion of southeast Kentucky, including the following
counties, Floyd, Knott, Letcher, Perry and Pike.

* WHEN...Until 900 PM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

training showers and thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing

Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued May 24 at 5:02PM CDT by NWS Fort Worth TX
properties.description:
At 502 PM CDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm 9
miles southwest of Gustine, or 13 miles southeast of Comanche, moving
southeast at 5 mph.

HAZARD...Winds in excess of 40 mph and half inch hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor damage to outdoor objects is
possible.

This storm will remain over mainly rural areas of west central
Hamilton, northeastern Mills and south central Comanche Counties,
including the following locations... Newburg, Energy, Van Dyke,
Hasse, Priddy, Sidney, Indian Gap, Pottsville, and Downing.
properties.instruction:
If outdoors, consider seeking shelter inside a building.

Torrential rainfall is also occurring with this storm and may lead to
localized flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded
roadways.

Frequent cloud to ground lightning is occurring with this storm.
Lightning can strike 10 miles away from a thunderstorm. Seek a safe
shelter inside a building or vehicle.

NWSheadline: A strong thunderstorm will impact portions of west central Hamilton, northeastern Mills and south central Comanche Counties through 545 PM CDT

properties.description:

* WHERE...In Delaware, Delaware Beaches. In New Jersey, Atlantic
Coastal Cape May and Coastal Atlantic.

* WHEN...Through Monday evening.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:

always have a floatation device with you and swim near a
lifeguard if possible. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float and do not swim against the current. If able, swim parallel
to the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the shore and call or
wave for help.

properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued May 24 at 4:00PM AST until May 26 at 6:00AM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
* WHAT...Life-threatening rip current.

* WHERE...Exposed beaches of northern and southeastern Puerto
Rico, Vieques, Culebra, and all the U.S. Virgin Islands.

* WHEN...Through late Monday night.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to
return to safety.
properties.instruction:
There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued May 24 at 11:38AM AKDT until May 26 at 1:00AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by ice jams, high water, and heavy ice runs
continues to be possible.

* WHERE...Lower Yukon River. This includes the communities of
Alakanuk, Emmonak, Kotlik, and Mountain Village.

* WHEN...Through late Monday night.

* IMPACTS...High water may result in flooding of rivers, creeks,
streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- As of Saturday evening, the River Watch Team reports the
breakup front is approximately 12 miles downstream of
Mountain Village. They observed local breakup at Emmonak and
Alakanuk with ice moving steadily through those communities.
As the breakup front works its way downstream Sunday into
Monday, residents in Nunam Iqua, Alakanuk, and Emmonak should
follow its progress closely. There is a long stretch of very
high water with abundant chunk ice behind the front that
should arrive in the next 2-3 days. Based on water levels
seen at the gauge at Pilot Station, these communities could
see the highest water levels since 1989.

- Http://www.weather.gov/aprfc

AQAHGX

The Texas Commission on Environmental Quality (TCEQ) has issued an
Ozone Action Day for the Houston, Galveston, and Brazoria area for
Monday, May 25, 2026.

Atmospheric conditions are expected to be favorable for producing
high levels of ozone pollution in the Houston, Galveston, and
surrounding areas on Monday. You can help prevent ozone pollution by
sharing a ride, walking, riding a bicycle, taking your lunch to work,
avoiding drive through lanes, conserving energy and keeping your vehicle
properly tuned.

emergency sign up form as well as links to fire restrictions at
weather.gov/medford/wildfire. One less spark, one less wildfire.

system. Familiarize yourself with your emergency plan and make
sure you listen to emergency services. Visit ready.gov/plan for
more information.

A Red Flag Warning is issued when we identify weather conditions
that promote rapid spread of fire which may become life-
threatening. This does not mean there is a fire. These conditions
are either occurring now or will begin soon. It is important to
have multiple ways to receive information from authorities.

properties.description:
...GUSTY RANGELAND WINDS AHEAD OF COLD FRONT...

Continued warm and very dry conditions ahead of a cold front on
the afternoon and evening of Memorial Day could create a critical
fire weather pattern as pre-frontal winds increase. Following
conditions tomorrow we will see good RH recovery overnight with a
30-40% chance of wetting rains through the rest of the week.

The National Weather Service in Boise has issued a Fire Weather
Watch for winds and low relative humidities, which is in effect
from Monday afternoon through Monday evening.

* AFFECTED AREA...In Oregon, Fire Weather Zone 672 Southern
Grasslands.

* TIMING...From Monday afternoon through Monday evening.

* WINDS...Southwest 20 to 25 mph with gusts up to 40 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...11 to 15 percent.

* TEMPERATURES...80 to 88 degrees.

* IMPACTS...Any fire that develops will catch and spread
quickly. Outdoor burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
A Fire Weather Watch means that critical fire weather conditions
are possible. Listen for later forecasts and possible Red Flag
Warnings.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued May 24 at 12:25PM EDT by NWS Gray ME
properties.description:
* Temperatures this Holiday weekend may cause people to
underestimate the dangers of the cold water temperatures which are
currently only in the mid 50s across Sebago Lake and Lake
Winnipesaukee, and in the mid 50s in the regions smaller lakes and
rivers.

* The cold water temperatures can quickly cause hypothermia to
anyone immersed in the water. When the water temperature is below
60 degrees, the average submerged person could loose dexterity
within minutes and be unable to accomplish simple tasks. Anyone
on small boats, canoes, or kayaks should plan accordingly if
recreating this weekend and use extreme caution to avoid this
threat. Paddle smart from the start and always wear your life

properties.areaDesc: Pribilof Islands
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued May 24 at 5:04AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
An unseasonably strong storm system for this time of year will
bring strong winds and gusts to the Pribilof Islands beginning
late this evening. Expect winds to quickly increase late this
afternoon with sustained easterly winds of 20 to 35 mph with gusts
of 45 to 60 mph, becoming more northeasterly by Monday evening.
Snow or rain/snow may produce areas of blowing snow at times
overnight tonight. Winds will likely peak early Monday morning
before slowly diminishing through late Monday evening. As the
storm moves east of the area Monday evening, winds will shift,
becoming northwesterly with gusts of 35 to 45 mph likely through
Wednesday before finally winding down.

NWSheadline: UNSEASONABLY STRONG WINDS FROM LATE THIS EVENING THROUGH MONDAY EVENING

properties.areaDesc: Unalaska and Nikolski
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued May 24 at 5:04AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
An unseasonably strong storm system for this time of year will
bring strong winds and gusts to Nikolski, Unalaska, and Akutan
beginning early this evening. Expect winds to quickly increase
this afternoon with sustained southeasterly winds of 20 to 35 mph
with gusts of 45 to 60 mph, becoming more southerly by Monday
morning. Winds will likely peak overnight tonight into Monday
morning before slowly diminishing through late Monday afternoon.
As the storm moves east of the area Monday evening, winds will
shift, becoming southwesterly with gusts of 35 to 45 mph likely
through Wednesday before finally winding down.

NWSheadline: UNSEASONABLY STRONG WINDS FROM EARLY THIS EVENING THROUGH MONDAY EVENING

properties.areaDesc: Aleutians East Borough
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued May 24 at 5:04AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
An unseasonably strong storm system for this time of year will
bring strong winds and gusts from Akutan to Sand Point and Nelson
Lagoon to beginning overnight tonight into early Monday morning.
Expect winds to quickly increase after midnight with sustained
southeasterly winds of 20 to 35 mph with gusts of 45 to 60 mph,
becoming more southerly by Monday afternoon. Gusts to 70 mph are
possible for Cold Bay Monday morning. Winds will likely peak by
mid morning Monday morning before slowly diminishing through
Monday night. As the storm moves east of the area Tuesday morning,
winds will shift, becoming westerly with gusts of 35 to 45 mph
likely through Wednesday before finally winding down.

NWSheadline: UNSEASONABLY STRONG WINDS FROM EARLY MONDAY MORNING THROUGH MONDAY EVENING

properties.areaDesc: Atka and Adak
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued May 24 at 5:04AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
An unseasonably strong storm system for this time of year will
bring strong winds and gusts to Adak and Atka beginning early
this morning. Expect winds to quickly increase after sunrise
this with sustained easterly winds of 30 to 45 mph with gusts of
50 to 65 mph. Winds will likely peak around mid afternoon before
slowly diminishing through late tonight. There will be lull in
the strong winds overnight tonight into Monday morning before
winds shift to the northwest and increase in intensity. Expect
northwest winds 20 to 35 mph with gusts up to 50 mph late Monday
morning through Monday evening. This second round of gusty winds
will slowly diminish overnight Monday into Tuesday before finally
winding down by Tuesday night.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued May 24 at 5:55AM EDT by NWS Caribou ME
properties.description:
* The warm air temperatures this weekend in the mid 60s to low
70s may cause people to underestimate the dangers of the cold
water temperatures which are currently only around 50 degrees on
Moosehead Lake and in the middle to upper 50s on smaller lakes
and rivers.

* The cold water temperatures can quickly cause hypothermia to
anyone immersed in the water. According to the Maine Warden
Service, when the water temperature is below 60 degrees, the
average submerged person could lose dexterity within minutes and
be unable to accomplish simple tasks. Anyone on small boats,
canoes or kayaks should plan accordingly if recreating this
weekend and use extreme caution to avoid this threat. Paddle
smart from the start and always wear your life jacket!

properties.areaDesc: Koror Palau Coastal Waters; Yap Coastal Waters; Chuuk Coastal Waters
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued May 24 at 4:50PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
A tropical disturbance, known as JTWC's Invest 99W, is currently
centered near 6N142E, just west of Eauripik. Although 99W remains
broad and disorganized, convection has rapidly improved over the last
day. Invest 99W is also connected to the monsoon trough to the
south, bringing a fresh surge of westerly winds, which will allow it
to organize. This convective structure is leading to a large area of
numerous to widespread showers and isolated thunderstorms, and choppy
seas across Chuuk and Yap State. Invest 99W remains rated sub-low by
the JTWC, which means development into a significant tropical
cyclone is not expected within the next few days.

As Invest 99W lifts northward this week, a monsoon tail will
intensify on the south side. Westerly to southwesterly winds of 20 to
30 kts will be possible along with seas hazardous to small craft.
Guidance continues to show this region as a narrow band displaced
from both Yap's and Palau's coastal waters, with seas remaining below
10 feet through Wednesday. As the system shifts further away, the
monsoon tail may transition into an inflow tail with southerly flow.
This could bring seas near hazardous conditions to Yap's coastal
waters late this week.

Residents and mariners should monitor the latest forecasts for the
region at weather.gov/gum/PublicForecasts and any information shared
by WSO Palau, WSO Yap, and WSO Chuuk for the local regions. For more
information on Invest 99W, see bulletins issued by JTWC under WMO
header ABPW10 PGTW and WTPN21 PGTW.

NWSheadline: A DEVELOPING DISTURBANCE MAY BRING HEAVY DOWNPOURS...GUSTY WINDS...AND CHOPPY SEAS THE NEXT FEW DAYS

properties.areaDesc: Unalaska and Nikolski
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued May 23 at 1:40PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
An unseasonably strong storm system for this time of year will
bring strong winds and gusts to Nikolski, Unalaska, and Akutan
beginning early Sunday evening. Expect winds to quickly increase
Sunday afternoon with sustained southeasterly winds of 20 to 35
mph with gusts of 45 to 60 mph, becoming more southerly by Monday
morning. Winds will likely peak overnight Sunday into Monday
morning before slowly diminishing through late Monday afternoon.
As the storm moves east of the area Monday evening, winds will
shift, becoming southwesterly with gusts of 35 to 45 mph likely
through Wednesday before finally winding down.

NWSheadline: UNSEASONABLY STRONG WINDS FROM EARLY SUNDAY EVENING THROUGH MONDAY EVENING

properties.areaDesc: Aleutians East Borough
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued May 23 at 1:40PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
An unseasonably strong storm system for this time of year will
bring strong winds and gusts from Akutan to Sand Point and Nelson
Lagoon to beginning overnight Sunday into early Monday morning.
Expect winds to quickly increase after midnight with sustained
southeasterly winds of 20 to 35 mph with gusts of 45 to 60 mph,
becoming more southerly by Monday afternoon. Gusts to 70 mph are
possible for Cold Bay Monday morning. Winds will likely peak
by mid morning Monday morning before slowly diminishing through
Monday night. As the storm moves east of the area Tuesday morning,
winds will shift, becoming westerly with gusts of 35 to 45 mph
likely through Wednesday before finally winding down.

NWSheadline: UNSEASONABLY STRONG WINDS FROM EARLY MONDAY MORNING THROUGH MONDAY EVENING

properties.areaDesc: Atka and Adak
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued May 23 at 1:40PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
An unseasonably strong storm system for this time of year will
bring strong winds and gusts to Adak and Atka beginning early
Sunday morning. Expect winds to quickly increase after sunrise
Sunday with sustained easterly winds of 30 to 45 mph with gusts of
50 to 65 mph. Winds will likely peak around mid afternoon before
slowly diminishing through late Sunday night. There will be a lull
in the strong winds overnight Sunday into Monday morning before
winds shift to the northwest and increase in intensity. Expect
northwest winds 20 to 35 mph with gusts up to 50 mph late Monday
morning through Monday evening. This second round of gusty winds
will slowly diminish overnight Monday into Tuesday before finally
winding down by Tuesday night.

NWSheadline: UNSEASONABLY STRONG WINDS FROM EARLY SUNDAY MORNING THROUGH MONDAY EVENING

properties.areaDesc: Pribilof Islands
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued May 23 at 1:40PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
An unseasonably strong storm system for this time of year will
bring strong winds and gusts to the Pribilof Islands beginning
late Sunday evening. Expect winds to quickly increase late Sunday
afternoon with sustained easterly winds of 20 to 35 mph with
gusts of 45 to 60 mph, becoming more northeasterly by Monday
evening. Winds will likely peak early Monday morning before
slowly diminishing through late Monday evening. As the storm
moves east of the area Monday evening, winds will shift, becoming
northwesterly with gusts of 35 to 45 mph likely through Wednesday
before finally winding down.

NWSheadline: UNSEASONABLY STRONG WINDS FROM LATE SUNDAY EVENING THROUGH MONDAY EVENING

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued May 23 at 2:25PM CDT by NWS Fort Worth TX
properties.description:
AQAFWD

The Texas Commission on Environmental Quality (TCEQ) has issued
an Ozone Action Day for the Dallas-Fort Worth area for Sunday,
May 24, 2026.

Atmospheric conditions are expected to be favorable for producing
high levels of ozone air pollution in the Dallas-Fort Worth area
on Sunday. You can help prevent ozone pollution by sharing a
ride, walking, riding a bicycle, taking your lunch to work,
avoiding drive-through lanes, conserving energy, and keeping your
vehicle properly tuned.

For more information on ozone:

properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued May 23 at 1:44AM MDT by NWS Billings MT
properties.description:
ESFBYZ

Unseasonably warm temperatures this weekend into early next week will
result in higher flows on area waterways through next week as the
remaining high elevation snowpack melts. Flooding is not expected at
this time. Rivers such as the Yellowstone and Clarks Fork of the
Yellowstone, Stillwater, and Boulder are expected to see flows double
the current rates by late in the week.

Smaller streams and creeks flowing out of the mountains will see
rises late this weekend into early next week, with larger rivers and
streams further downstream seeing the strongest increases from
Tuesday through Friday.

Those with interests along foothills waterways should be prepared for
higher water levels, and move property and livestock away from
rivers, streams, and low lying areas.

Recreationists in the mountains and foothills should be prepared for
changing conditions and use extra caution when near waterways. Flows
will be higher and faster, and the water is very cold. Cloudy water
conditions during runoff can also hide submerged hazards. Keep
children and pets away from the edge of fast flowing waterways.

Stay tuned to the forecast. Please report any flooding to local law
enforcement and have them relay the report to the National Weather
Service.

NWSheadline: Snowmelt Will Bring Higher Stream Flows

properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued May 24 at 5:07PM CDT until May 24 at 5:45PM CDT by NWS Twin Cities/Chanhassen MN
properties.description:
SVRMPX

The National Weather Service in the Twin Cities has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Northeastern Renville County in central Minnesota...

* Until 545 PM CDT.

* At 507 PM CDT, a severe thunderstorm was located 7 miles south of
Cosmos, or 17 miles west of Hutchinson, moving east at 20 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and quarter size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Hail damage to vehicles is expected. Expect wind damage to
roofs, siding, and trees.

* Locations impacted include...
Buffalo Lake and Lakeside.
properties.instruction:
Seek shelter inside a well-built structure and stay away from
windows. This storm is capable of producing damaging winds and large
hail.
